newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian commission takes up minister's sex case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian commission takes up minister's sex case.

text.p: A Belgian parliamentary commission met on Wednesday to decide whether Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo should be referred to court over allegations of sex with under-age boys.
The commission must determine whether there is enough evidence in a report on the case from the Brussels prosecutor- general to send Di Rupo before the Cour de Cassation, the country's highest court.

Di Rupo, a colourful 45-year-old francophone socialist, does not deny being a homosexual but says he had sex only with consenting adults. Homosexuality is not a crime in Belgium. Sex with children younger than 16 is.
Belgian radio said the 11 members of the panel would probably try to reach a decision on Wednesday.

Several Belgian papers said the 29-page report by the prosecutor contained detailed allegations against Di Rupo dating back to the late 1980s from a man, arrested in connection with a child porn video case, who was 15 at the time.
Newspaper commentators said pressure on Di Rupo to step down over the scandal was rising, although some expected the minister to fight to the end.
Most opposition politicians have stopped short of calling for Di Rupo's immediate resignation, but said he should step down if parliament lifts his immunity from prosecution.
Formally, the commission, made up of parliamentarians of the main parties, puts a recommendation on the Di Rupo case to parliament, which then votes on it in a full session.
The whole procedure is very similar to the one that brought down Belgian NATO Secretary General Willy Claes last year.
Parliament referred him to the Cour de Cassation over allegations of bribery in an army contract in the late 1980s. He has still not been tried.
Under Belgian law a minister can be questioned, confronted by witnesses or prosecuted, and his property searched, only once a full session of the lower house has voted to lift his immunity.
A date for a parliamentary vote on the commission's recommendation has not yet been set. A simple majority of the 150-seat house is needed to implement the commission's advice.
Parliament has three options when it comes to a vote:
-- It can adopt the prosecutor's request and bring Di Rupo before the Cour de Cassation. This would be likely to end his career.
-- It can vote for a continuation of the investigation. This could be seen as a stay of execution but would remove none of the pressure on Di Rupo to consider his position in the cabinet.

The accusation against Di Rupo follows an unconnected scandal of paedophile abduction, sexual abuse and murder that has shaken Belgium to the core since the arrest of convicted rapist Marc Dutroux in mid-August.
Ensuing revelations of police and judicial bungling, incompetence and suggestions of political interference have shattered public confidence in the legal and political system.
